pages.name: Introduction
pages.html:
Character Creation: Character creation is a game unto itself, in which the player rolls for their starting characteristics and chooses their career paths and determines how they develop. A player can choose to stop working, in order to pursue life as a spacer, anytime they finish a term of a career.

  • A Note on Gender: The character can choose to be whatever gender they feel is meaningful to them. There are no mechanical advantages or disadvantages for being any gender.

Character Creation Procedure

Use the table on the opposite page to facilitate character creation.

1) Generate Characteristics: Roll 2D to determine each Characteristic.

2) Enlist in a Career: Use the following sub-steps to determine the career path. Use the Service Table on the opposite page in conjunction with this step of character creation.

  • A) Choose a Career and Attempt to Enlist. If failed, become drafted.
  • B) Acquire Career Skill: Roll on one of the applicable career Skill or education tables and gain the Skill at Rank 1 or increase the Skill by +1 rank if already acquired on pg. 17.
    • B1) First Term Only: Acquire one Service Skill and one Professional Education Skill at rank 0, along with the Enlistment Skill for the career if it's your first term in your first career only. You do not roll to acquire a Skill for the first term.
  • C) Roll Survival: If successful, move to sub-step D. If failed, roll on the Injury Table and move to Step 3 if possible. If you survive, advance four years.
    • C1) Optional- Roll event: If you succeeded in surviving, roll on the event table for your career type. If using events, you must use them for the entire duration of character creation. Events are on pages 22-25.
  • D) If Military, Roll to Rank. Skip this step in your first drafted military term.
    • D1) Commission: If you gain a rank, you may choose to commission if it's your first term in this military career. Failure to do either keeps the character at their current rank. You cannot commission past your first non-drafted military career term unless an event says otherwise.
  • E) Aging: Advance four years in age. If four terms deep into a career (age 34 or higher when starting this career term), determine aging effects on Characteristics by using the Aging table and rolling the required saves to prevent decreases in Characteristics. See pg. 18 for more

3) Continue Career?: The player determines if they want their character to continue working and find a new career or if they want to stop and become a free-lancing spacer.

  • Continue Career: Must roll to reenlist to continue in the same career.
  • Success: If reenlisted, return to Step 2B
  • Failure: If failed to reenlist, choose a new career for at least one term.
  • Start Spacing: Move onto step four, and finish character creation.

4) Muster Out: When leaving a career, a player musters out of their career and receives some form of compensation for their services. See page 19 for more information.

  • If the PC served multiple terms in the same career, then muster out using the Mustering Out tables a number of times equal to the amount of terms, alternating rolling on each column.

Book p.16

pages.name: Characteristic Generation
pages.html:
Step 1) Characteristic Generation: Roll 2D to determine the following Characteristic scores. The average Characteristic score is 7.

  • Strength (STR): The level of physical strength a character has.
  • Dexterity (DEX): This represents a character's coordination, agility, and mobility.
  • Endurance (END): This represents the stamina and ruggedness of a character.
  • Intelligence (INT): This represents the level of reason and understanding a character has.
  • Education (EDU): This represents the level of education a character has. It can also be seen as their ability to learn and retain information.
  • Social Standing (SOC): This represents the level of societal privilege you have, typically due to your family and/or your connections within your culture. Anyone with a 10+ will have a noble title.

Physical Characteristics: Strength, Dexterity, and Endurance represents the physical characteristics.

Mental Characteristics: Intelligence, Education, and Social level represent the mental characteristics.

Dice Modifiers: Each Characteristic score will have a Dice Modifier, which is applied when rolling dice that use those corresponding Characteristics.

Step 2A) Enlistment

When enlisted for the first term of their career at age 18, a character will gain one Skill at rank 0 as determined by the career.

  • Navy: Characters who enlist in the navy are trained in spacefaring military services. All enlisted characters automatically gain Vaccsuit 0.
  • Marines: Enlisting in the marines allows for specialized military training to be space marines. Marines are the primary soldiers found on starships. However, some marines with advanced training perform small-scale operations such as boarding starships, clandestine operations, and other covert operations. All enlisted marines automatically gain Melee Combat 0.
  • Army: Army enlistment allows for general military training and advanced education. The army makes up the bulk of terrestrial forces during conflicts and occupations. All enlisted army personnel automatically gain Gun Combat 0.
  • Scouts: Scouts are sent out to remote areas to chart space lanes, survey planets and populations, and provide law enforcement for frontier communities. All enlisted scouts gain Pilot 0.
  • Merchants: Characters who enlist in the merchants are trained in trade and economics while on a merchant ship. All enlisted merchants gain Broker 0.
  • Civilian: Characters who initially pursue a less adventurous career are able to choose the focus of their profession. Some examples are civil services, logistics, law enforcement, labor sector, white collar, or anything else the player would like to imagine. An enlisted civilian character gains Profession 0.

Step 2A1) Drafted

Failure to enlist forces the character to become drafted. Anyone drafted is assumed to be placed into immediate military or security training. If drafted into the merchants, the character is assumed to be assigned to the merchant marines, who may see combat. Being drafted into civilians means the character is assumed to be placed into a security group/militia or labor jobs, to fill in gaps. The automatic Skill acquired for drafted characters is Gun Combat 0.

Book p.18

pages.html:

  • Skill Rank: When gaining a skill during a career, the character acquired it at rank 1, unless doing basic training. If the character already has the skill from basic training or enlistment at rank 0, it increases to rank 1.
  • Basic Training: Only for the first term of a character’s generation, the player chooses one Skill from Service Skills and Professional Education tables at Rank 0 instead of rolling for Skill acquisition.

pages.name: Promotion and Commission
pages.html:
Step 2D) Promotion and Commission: Characters in a military career can check to see if they gain a rank while serving. These checks can only be made once per term. Drafted characters cannot roll to be promoted during their first military term.

  • Military Rank: All military personnel start at Rank 0. The benefit of ranking allows for extra mustering rolls when they leave the service, as determined by their rank.
    • For example; at Rank 1, a character gets an extra mustering out roll, while at rank 3, they gain two extra mustering out rolls when they leave their military career.
  • Commission: Commissioned officers benefit from being able to roll on the Commissioned Officer Skills table once per term in place of rolling on one of the other available Skill tables. Commissioned characters gain a +1DM on mustering out rolls, as determined by their rank.
    • For example; A commissioned officer of rank 2 can apply a +1DM to a single mustering roll of their choice when they leave their career while a commissioned officer for rank 4 can apply +1DM to two separate mustering rolls of their choice.
  • Making a check to gain commission can only be made once per career. If a character fails the commission roll, it cannot be made again.

Consult the Rank Benefits table when mustering out to see what benefits of rank and commission are offered.

pages.name: Reenlisting
pages.html:
Step 3) Reenlisting: To continue in a career, the character must reenlist.

  • Success: A success represents signing on for a new career or being valued at your job - for now.
  • Failure: If failed to reenlist, choose a new career for at least one term. This represents being laid off, a contract expiring, or discharged from service.
  • A character can choose to leave a career instead or reenlist, if so they move onto Step 4 to muster out but then return to Step 2 to start a new career.

Book p.20

pages.name: Mustering Out
pages.html:
Step 4) Mustering Out: Use the following tables to roll muster out benefits when leaving a career.

  • Material Benefits: Material benefits represent non-cash goods a character takes with them when leaving a career.
  • Monetary Benefits: A maximum of three rolls is allowed on this table per character in a single career for terms 2, 4, and 6. All remaining rolls must be done on the Material Benefits table.

When Mustering out, roll 1D per term served in a career. If the character acquired a DM to a muster roll during their career, apply it to a single applicable roll.

Book p.20

pages.name: Material and Monetary Benefits
pages.html:
The Following Are Descriptions of Each Material Benefit:

  • Characteristic Score Increase: The listed characteristic increases by +1.
  • Low Passage: The spacer is granted access to a redeemable ticket for low passage on a trip of their choice, usable once.
  • Medium Passage: The spacer is granted access to a redeemable ticket for medium passage on a trip of their choice, usable once.
  • High Passage: The spacer is granted access to a redeemable ticket for high passage on a trip of their choice, usable once.
  • Gun: The spacer receives a single firearm upon leaving the service. The weapon must be a Body Pistol (short), Carbine (Stock), or Energy Pistol (Energy), depending on the spacer’s training, as listed in parenthesis. If the spacer only has Ranged Combat 0, then they muster out with a Body Pistol by default.
  • Blade: The spacer musters out with a Dagger. if the spacer has Melee Combat (Blade), then they are able to muster out with a One-Handed Sword.
  • Ship Shares: Ship Share represents a discount on a downpayment for starship, provided as credit, scrip, or favors the character can call on when purchasing a ship. When gaining a ship share, roll 1D. The result represents the discount in cost used towards a downpayment for a starship. For example; if a 3 is rolled on 1D, then the character can cash in their ship shares to get 3% off the 20% downpayment needed for a starship— decreasing the required downpayment to 17% of the total starship cost. See Starship Construction for more information regarding starship purchase.
  • Spacer Support Service (SSS): The SSS (referred to as Triple-S) functions as a private organization that provides working spacers certain perks. When a spacer is in a Type A or B spaceport, they will have access to the local SSS Hostel for one week stay once a month.
  • SSS Continued: The SSS also provides up to a 10,000cr per year stipend for medical care and legal support per year, as long as they seek such aid in a type A or B starport. Membership is non-transferrable and is considered a life-time perk as long as the spacer acts within the expected behavior of the SSS. Causes for removal from the SSS are 1) killing of a fellow law-abiding SSS member, 2) stealing the ID of another SSS member, 3) loaning the ID to a non-SSS member, or 4) being found guilty of piracy.
  • Starship: If mustering out with a starship, it is considered a used ship from that career that the character is now responsible for but is under commission of the service it left from. This means the spacer doesn’t own it outright but is using it on loan from the service. Every time this benefit is rolled, increase the age of the ship by 10 years, where one result represents 10 years of service, two results are 20 years of service, etc. All ships of 40 years in age are officially decommissioned from the loaned service, meaning the character will own the ship outright. The character is still responsible for the maintenance and fuel costs, but the referee can apply reimbursement from fuel receipts from the service if they want to involve bureaucratic paperwork into their game.
    • Scout Ship: This represents the stock 100 ton scout ship on pg. 69. A scout ship doesn’t have monthly loans but the character in possession of it is still responsible for all maintenance, fuel, and operational costs to keep it in service. Possession of a scout ship makes the character “on-call” for per diem work in the scout service anytime, with a chance of being called to service on a 10+ roll whenever they stop at a scout base starports of A, B, or C classification. Having a commissioned scout starship provides free refined fuel at scout bases and housing.
    • Merchant Ship: A merchant ship is a used 200T trader, on pg. 69, that the character was provided by a prior colleague, outfitted for all general trade and passengers. The character is responsible for a 150,000cr monthly loan for the remainder of the ship’s loan period, along with other operational costs.

pages.name: Pension
pages.html:
Pensions: When a character manages to maintain staying in the same career for 5 or more terms, they will receive a monthly pension for their services in addition to their mustering out benefits. The character must choose to either accrue their pension monthly or get a lump sum yearly which can be collected in their bank account at any A-type or B-type Starport.

  • Monthly: New Monthly amounts are only able to be collected from the character’s account at the beginning of the universal month period (30 Earth days).
  • Yearly: Yearly accounts total to less than a monthly amount due to transfer fees and tax deductions from a lump sum transfer.

When a Character receives a pension, they must select monthly or yearly deposits. Use the following table to determine a pension a character receives:

pages.name: Example of Character Creation
pages.html:
The following is a breakdown of character creation. Please note: this didn’t incorporate the optional events into character generation.

Generation: The player rolls 2D for each stat and gets a UPC of 899678. The player names their character Sofiya Chen and assigns them a homeworld of Gagarin-3

Term 1: Sofiya Chen is 18 years old and chooses to enlist in the Navy, which requires an 8+.

  • Enlist: The player rolls 2D+INT DM (+0) and gets 10, success!
  • Career Skills; Enlistment Skill and Basic training (term 1 only): Sofiya gains the following: Vaccsuit-0 for enlisting. Since this is her first career term ever, she is able to choose two skills at zero rank. She selects Ranged Combat-0 from the service skills table and Comms-0 from the professional education table.
  • Survival: Next, Sofiya must see if she survives her first term in the Navy without injury (or worse!). The player rolls 2D and adds INT DM (+0) and must roll a 5+ and gets a 7, success!
  • Promotion: Sofiya would like to see if she was promoted from rank 0 (Private) to rank 1 (Ensign) in the Navy and must roll a 8+ with a EDU DM (+0), and roll an 8. Sofiya is now an ensign!
  • Commission: Now that Sofiya is an ensign, she will attempt to see if she can gain commission. Sofiya’s player must roll a 10+ modified by SOC (+0) and roll a 4, failure! Sofiya cannot be a commissioned naval officer.
  • Age and Reenlistment: Sofiya Now increases in age by four years and is now 22. She can decide to stay in the navy or leave and pursue a new career. She decided to attempt another term in the navy, so she must roll a 6+ and get a 7, success! She gained another term of the Navy.

Term 2: Sofiya Chen is now 22, is a private, and her UPC is 899678 and has Vaccsuit-0, Ranged combat-0, and Comms-0

  • Career Skill: Sofiya learns a skill during her second term. The player can choose to roll on the Navy column on the personal Development Table, Service Skills table, or professional education table. The player chooses to roll on the service skills table. They roll 1D and rolls a 1, which is Pilot. Since this isn’t Sofiya's first career term ever, she gains the skill at rank-1.
  • Survival: Sofiya’s player must determine if a mishap happens to her character. She must roll 2D and get a 5+, and succeeds!
  • Promotion: Sofiya attempts to gain another promotion, and needs an 8+ to succeed. Unfortunately, she gets a 7 so she doesn't get promoted past private during this career term.
  • Age and Reenlistment: Sofiya increases in age by four years and is now 26. Sofiya’s player decides that she will muster out of the Navy, thinking it might be a dead end for her.
  • Muster Out: since Sofiya has served two terms, she rolls once on each mustering out table. First is the Material benefits table and rolls 1D and gets Blade and rolls 1D on the monetary benefits and receives 5000cr. Since she was a private, she earned a bonus mustering out on the material benefits table and gains +2 EDU.

Now that Sofiya has finished her career, she can choose to start a new career or begin a life of spacing. Sofiya decides to become a spacer, finalising her character:

  • Sofiya Chen, age 26, former Navy Private. UPC: 899698 Vaccsuit-0, Ranged Combat-0, Comms-0, Pilot-1

Book p.22

pages.name: Life Events, Military
pages.html:
Optional, Life Events

When a character survives a term in a career, they roll to determine what event transpires during the four-year term of their career. Using these optional tables are designed to provide more choice in character creation and provide narrative consequences for those choices.

  • Choosing to use Life Events should be determined at the beginning of character creation and should be used for the entirety of the creation process, due to the variables that may impact character progression.
  • PTSD: If a character gains PTSD during an event, roll D3 to determine which attribute is affected: 1) INT 2) EDU 3) SOC. The rolled attribute will then decrease in score by D3.

Military Life Events

Use this table for characters who are in Army, Navy, or Marine careers. Add +1per additional term in a career after the first. For example, on your second term, roll 1D+1 on the events table.

1DEvent
1Chewed Up and Spat Out: You barely make it out of basic training and struggle to find a role in the military. You are unceremoniously discharged from service and can only enter military service again if drafted.
2Voluntold: Your superiors are looking for “volunteers” for a hard labor engineering mission on a remote outpost, but you are too low of rank to safely say no. If you say no, incur -2DM to reenlistment. If you say yes, roll 8+ on a STR check.
- Success: You were able to demonstrate that not only that you are a team player but also capable of being dependable for physical demands. Increase STR by +1.
- Failure: You show that you are a team player, but you have an accident! Roll D3+3 on the Injury table to determine how you are injured.
3Up for Promotion: You are automatically promoted to rank. If you are currently rank 1 or higher and are not commissioned, then you are automatically commissioned as well.
4Espionage: You are offered a chance to leak secrets for financial benefit. Roll 8+ on an INT check.
- Success: You slyly slip secrets out to the client and are paid 2D x 2000cr and gain a Contact.
- Failure: You are incarcerated for D3 terms and do not benefit from any muster rolls from this career. See prison for more information.
5Warzone: It finally happened; you were sent to the front lines. Roll 8+ on a DEX check to determine what happens.
- Success of 12: You demonstrate heroism on the battlefield and are automatically promoted a rank and can increase a known Skill by 1 rank.
- Success 8-11: Your boots-on-the-ground experiences allow you to perform a Skill you know. Increase a known Skill by 1 rank.
- Failure 3-7: You are injured. Roll 1D+1 on the Injury table but gain 1 rank in a Skill you know. Unfortunately, you are discharged from the service after sustaining the injury, preventing you from reenlistment into this service.
- Failure of 2: You are killed in battle. You are granted a post-mortem promotion and are buried with honors.
6Honor Duel: You are challenged to a duel by a rival officer. If you are not an officer, your superior officer forces you to fight on their behalf. Roll 8+ on a DEX check.
- Result of 12+: You severely injure the officer, forcing them to retire early. You are immediately promoted while gaining an Enemy in the opposing officer.
- Success range 8-11: You defeat the officer and are promoted for your demonstration of arms. Gain a Rival in the opposing officer.
- Failure range 3-7: You are defeated. Roll D3+3 on the Survival Table and gain a Rival.
- Failure 2 or less: Roll D3 on the survival table and gain an Enemy.
7Extracurricular Training: You have driven yourself to improve a Skill you have to become better than what basic training provided you. Roll 8+ on an EDU Check.
- Success: Increase one of your lowest ranked Skills by +1.
- Failure: You are seen as isolated due to your determination. You still gain a +1 in a Skill, but if you had an Ally or Connection, you lose them. Otherwise, you gain a Rival.
8Peacekeeper: You are assigned to a peacekeeping mission to maintain relations between two factions. Roll 8+ on an EDU check.
- Success: You ended up pencil pushing for a term. Earn one Civilian Skill at rank 0 or increase a current civilian Skill by +1 rank.
- Failure: Conflict breaks out, and you are caught in the middle. Roll 1D on the survival table.
9Court Marshal: You find yourself accused of betrayal to the service and will be subjected to a tribunal. You are brought to trial to defend yourself. You can choose to hire a lawyer for 1D x 1000Cr who provides a +D3 DM to the trial check. You must have the money and cannot take on debt for hiring a lawyer.
The trial: Roll 8+ on a SOC check; add any lawyer bonus you may have.
- Success: The accusations are thrown out, and you are able to continue your career, with an automatic reenlistment for another term for your current service.
- Failure: You lose your job and are imprisoned for D3 terms. You do not gain any mustering benefits from your job due to your criminal record.
Result of 2: You are executed without honors.
10Shell-Shocked: Your experience has led you to see the horrors of war. Friends have perished before your eyes and the perpetual exposure to violence has strained your nerves. You unfortunately lose an Ally or Contact due to the tragic event if you have one. Roll 8+ on an END check.
- Success: You are able to prevent the grim reality from fraying your mind. Gain +1 END.
- Failure: You gain PTSD and are given medical discharge. You cannot enlist in any military career.
11War Hero: On a tour of duty, you found yourself up against unimaginable odds. You made an important call to get yourself out of there and your comrades. Roll 8+ on one of the following checks:
- STR for Army
- DEX for Marines
- INT for Navy
- EDU if an officer of any military branch
On a success: Immediately be promoted one rank and get a +1 DM to one mustering out roll.
On a failure: Immediately promoted but incur an injury. Roll D3 on the Injury table.
12Career Soldier: The military has become your life, and you are well integrated into its bureaucratic structure. Your faith in following protocol is questioned when a superior orders you and your comrades into a dangerous situation. You can choose to follow orders or defy orders.
Follow Orders: Roll 8+ on a INT check.
- Success: You are sent into the fray to complete the mission at the grave cost of your buddies. You are automatically promoted one rank, but gain an Enemy in a former surviving comrade while also gaining one Contact in the higher ranks of the military.
- Failure: You are promoted but sustain a significant injury. Roll D3 on the Injury table.
Defy Orders: Roll 8+ on a SOC check.
- Success: You defy orders and develop a new strategy to keep your comrades alive while finishing the operation. Top brass frowns upon defying orders but begrudgingly promote you one rank, but you incur a -2DM to reenlistment. You gain one Rival in the demoted former superior officer who gave the order.
- Failure: You defy orders but aren't able to complete the mission, leading to the inevitable death of a majority of your comrades and the loss of rank for your superior. You are court marshalled; roll 8+ on a SOC check. A success means you are discharged from service. Failure means you are dishonorably discharged and lose all mustering out benefits, while also being jailed for D3 terms. Regardless of the outcome, you gain one Ally in a former comrade for defying military orders while also gaining one Enemy in the demoted military officer.
13+Unique: Roll 1D and determine the unique event that occurs during your current career term. Add +1 to the 1D roll for every term served past term 8. For example, if rolling on term 9, roll 1D+1 on the following:
  1. Life Among Sophonts: Your job has allowed you the privilege to work with a different intelligent species, forming meaningful connections and a deeper knowledge of your place in the universe. Gain one Non-Human Ally and Linguistics 1 OR Science 1. if you already have either of those Skills, increase its rank by +1.
  2. Psionic Encounter: You have an encounter with a hidden psion, unlocking your potential to become psychic. Use the Unlocking Psionic Potential procedure to determine if you are now psionic.
  3. Influential Contact: You gain an influential contact within the largest government in the subsector.
  4. Artefact: You stumbled upon an ancient artefact that may be of significant value. You must find a specialist to determine its worth when you begin spacing.
  5. Social Isolation: As you age, you start to lose more and more friends due to career changes, lifestyle choices, or death. You lose one Ally or Contact. If you have none, then decrease SOC by -D3.
  6. Forced Retirement: You are forced out of service due to age. You may not reenlist with any career due to your age, regardless of your experience.

Book p.24-25

pages.name: Life Events, Non-military
pages.html:
Use this table to determine events for characters who are in Scouts, Merchants, or Civilian careers. Add +1DM per additional term in a career after the first. For example, on your second term, roll 1D+1 on the events table.

1DEvent
1Severe Illness: During your first term in this career, you succumbed to a debilitating illness. Roll 8+ on an END check.
- Success: You overcome the illness without it impacting your work.
- Failure: You are unceremoniously fired from the job and cannot attempt to reenlist next term.
2Inheritance: Someone you know passes on, and you are surprised that you gained an inheritance from them. Roll 1D. Odd results are material benefits (Merchant Column) and even results are monetary benefits (Civilian Column). Immediately roll 1D+1 on the associated muster column to determine what you gain from the inheritance.
3Management: Your superiors assign an important task that must be completed by a certain deadline. Roll 8+ on a INT check.
- Success: You are deemed an important lackey by management and reward you with a +1DM when you muster out.
- Failure: You fail terribly, and management isn't amused. You are fired from your job; muster out.
4Romantic Interest: You meet someone special but must balance your grueling work with being a good partner. Roll 8+ on an EDU check.
- Success: You are able to figure out a healthy balance. Gain +1 SOC and an Ally.
- Failure: You are selfish and unreliable. Gain -1 SOC and an Enemy.
5On Strike: There is a labor strike at your career, and you are asked to join the other employees in striking.
- Refuse to strike: You decide to become a scab for work. Roll 8+ on a DEX check to not get caught. On a success, you gain 1D x 2000cr and +1DM on any muster roll for this career. You are automatically reenlisted and promoted (if applicable) but are considered a class traitor and gain a Rival from the striking leadership.
- Join the struggle: You gain an Ally in the form of a fellow worker. You now are part of the contract negotiation. Roll 8+ on a SOC check. Success: You succeed at negotiations and now roll +1 to all cash benefit rolls from this career when mustering out. Failure: You hit a negotiation stalemate and nothing significant changes. Reenlistment roll now incurs -2DM.
6Secret: You learn a rumour that there will be a shake-up in management between two rival superiors, with one of them getting fired. What do you do?
- Nothing: You try to keep your head down and let it blow over. Roll 8+ on an SOC check. You are not affected by the shake-up. On a failure, you are associated with the terminated management and are fired.
- Tell the Manager: Roll 8+ on an INT check. On a success, you tell the correct superior and are automatically reinlisted and gain an Ally. On a failure, you blab to the wrong superior. You gain -2DM to your reenlistment roll due to being considered having poor discernment, and gain a Rival.
7Made Redundant: During your career, downsizing at your place of work became inevitable. Roll 8+ on a SOC check.
- Success: Automatically reenlist in the career for another term.
- Failure: You are terminated. Gain only the cash benefit from this career when mustering out.
8Heated Rivalry: You have a friendly rivalry with someone you work with. One day, management assigns a task that is in direct competition with a coworker to keep your job. You can choose to either compete to let the coworker take the task. What do you do?
- Selflessly pass it along: You are terminated from your job but gain an Ally in your former rival.
- Try to Defeat Them: Roll 8+ on an EDU check:
- Success: You defeat your coworker and get them fired. You are automatically reenlisted and gain +1DM to any one muster roll when mustering out but gain an Enemy.
- Failure: You are crushed by your rival and are terminated from your job but gain a Rival and a +1DM to a single mustering out benefit of your choice.
9Legal Trouble: You find yourself accused of some form of criminal behaviour that you swear you are innocent of. You are brought to trial to defend yourself. You can choose to hire a lawyer for 1D x 1000Cr, who provides a +D3 DM to the trial check. You must have the money and cannot take on debt for hiring a lawyer.
The trial: Roll 8+ on a SOC check. Add any lawyer bonus you may have.
- Success: You get off without issue.
- Failure: You are fined 2D x 5000Cr.
- Result of 2: You lose your job and are imprisoned for D3 terms. You do not gain any mustering benefits from your job due to your criminal record.
10Tragedy: A sudden event turns your life upside down. You must endure these turbulent times, which will strain your mental health. You unfortunately lose an Ally or Contact due to the tragic event, if you have one. Roll 8+ on an END check.
- Success: You are able to weather these trying times consuming your mind. Gain +1 END.
- Failure: You gain PTSD and are given medical discharge from your career.
11Local Hero: A crisis occurs where you live, whether it be environmental (Scout), economical (Merchant), or political (Civilian). You decide that you can provide help to others in need. Roll 8+ on the following checks:
END for Scouts
EDU for Civilians
SOC for Merchants
- Success: You demonstrate your adaptability and gain Jack-of-All-Trades 1 (or increase it by +1).
- Failure: Your noble attempt causes you an injury. Roll 1D on the Injury table.
12Married to the Job: All you know is this career, at the cost of a social life. You attempt to break out of the cage you built for yourself and try to make connections with others. Roll 8+ on a SOC check:
- Success: You gain an Ally in the form of a friend or romantic partner.
- Failure: You struggle to meet people and decide it's better to focus on work instead. You lose -1 SOC but gain an extra muster roll for this career.
13+Unique: Roll 1D and determine the unique event that occurs during your current career term. Add +1 to the 1D roll for every term served past term 8. For example, if rolling on term 9, roll 1D+1 on the following:
  1. Life Among Sophonts: Your job has allowed you the privilege to work with a different intelligent species, forming meaningful connections and a deeper knowledge of your place in the universe. Gain one Non-Human Ally and Linguistics 1 OR Science 1. if you already have either of those Skills, increase its rank by +1.
  2. Psionic Encounter: You have an encounter with a hidden psion, unlocking your potential to become psychic. Use the Unlocking Psionic Potential procedure to determine if you are now psionic.
  3. Influential Contact: You gain an influential contact within the largest government in the subsector.
  4. Artefact: You stumbled upon an ancient artefact that may be of significant value. You must find a specialist to determine its worth when you begin spacing.
  5. Social Isolation: As you age, you start to lose more and more friends due to career changes, lifestyle choices, or death. You lose one Ally or Contact. If you have none, then decrease SOC by -D3.
  6. Forced Retirement: You are forced out of service due to age. You may not reenlist with any career due to your age, regardless of your experience.

pages.name: Prison
pages.html:
Prison: When sent to prison, roll 1D on the following table to determine what events occur while imprisoned each term. Any character in prison must serve the entire prison sentence unless stated otherwise.

  • Prison Experience: All terms will automatically earn a Skill or increase a Skill by +1 rank if the character already has the Skill. Each term a character must make the required attribute check and may earn something from the term. Failure on this check indicates an injury due to hard prison labor, cruel and unusual punishment, systemic issues of prison management, or interprisoner conflicts.
  • Aging: Characters in prison are also affected by aging. For every term in prison in place of a career term starting a term 4, remember to make aging checks using the Aging table pg. 20.
1DEvent
1Hit the weights: Gain a Melee Skill of choice or Athlete.
Roll 8+ on a STR Check:
- Success: Join a prison gang and gain a Contact.
- Failure: Faulty equipment. Roll 1D on the Injury table.
2Block Runner: You become adept at moving goods and messages around the prison block. Gain gambling, stealth, or Melee combat (Blade).
Roll 8+ on a DEX check:
- Success: You gain a good reputation. Gain one Ally
- Failure: A mixup of goods led to a failure of a job. Roll 1D on the Injury table.
3Poor Conditions: You're forced to adapt to the harsh conditions of your prison. Gain Streetwise, Carouse, or Recon.
Roll 8+ on a END check:
- Success: Gain Jack-of-All-Trades 1.
- Failure: You unfortunately succumb to the harsh conditions. Roll 1D on the Injury table.
4Smart Guy: You adapt your prior knowledge to help you adapt to prison life. Gain Admin, Legal, or Profession.
Roll 8+ on a INT check:
- Success: You are able to help other prisoners with knowing their legal rights and gain a Contact.
- Failure: Prison admin frowns upon your cleverness. Roll 1D on the Injury table.
5Hit the Books: You've fully utilized the access to the prison's library and different classes offered to inmates. Gain Mechanic, Engineering, or Electronics.
Roll 8+ on a EDU check:
- Success: You successfully prove that you are capable of reentering society. You are released early and regain one of the muster rolls from your last career.
- Failure: You get caught up in a prison riot you weren't participating in. Roll 1D on the Injury table.
6Build Bridges: You learn to navigate the social hierarchy of the prison and attempt to integrate yourself into its structure. Gain Diplomacy, Deception, or Persuade.
Roll 8+ on a SOC check:
- Success: Your attempts have yielded you an Ally.
- Failure: You offend someone. Roll D3 on the Injury table.

Book p.27
